Monday, November 23, 2026

Governor Stein Announces Aerial Asset Accessibility Grant Program Is Taking Off

Raleigh

Nov 23, 2026

Today Governor Stein and North Carolina Emergency Management announced nine western North Carolina airports will receive more than $24 million through the 
Aerial Asset Accessibility Grant Program
 (AAAGP) that is administered by 
NC Emergency Management
 to repair Hurricane Helene damage and expand the airports’ ability to support emergency response when roads are closed. Seventeen airports submitted applications seeking approximately $72 million. Grants fund backup power, hangars, a new terminal, and fuel capacity at regional airports that served as lifelines after the storm.  
“Enhancing these nine western North Carolina airports is great news for our state’s ability to respond quickly to disasters,” 
said Governor Josh Stein. 
“We never know when the next storm will strike, but these investments will make us better prepared to respond to whatever may come.”  
After Helene, hundreds of roads were closed because of landslides, washouts, and downed trees, leaving many mountain communities isolated. General aviation airports became emergency logistics hubs, receiving and distributing essential supplies and moving first responders. Air traffic over western North Carolina rose 300% after the storm, according to NC Department of Transportation and Federal Aviation Administration data. Several awarded projects address gaps experienced during the response and recovery, such as fuel capacity and adequate hangar space used for logistical supplies. 
Grant recipients will repair, replace, and restore airport infrastructure damaged by Helene. They may also improve their capacity for emergency preparedness and disaster response through capital projects, infrastructure, and communication improvements on airfield property. The program is designed to add regional emergency response capacity at general aviation airports; airports that offer commercial passenger service are not eligible. Under eligibility rules 
set by the General Assembly
, an airport must have fuel available 24 hours a day, seven days a week; have on-site aviation mechanics who serve the public; be able to stay open around the clock during a state of emergency; and be located in a county that agrees to give the state access to facilities funded by the program. NCEM prioritized airports with the runway capacity, storage space, and staff to substantially strengthen regional disaster readiness and to accommodate aircraft of various types and sizes. 
Common improvements include the installation of standby generators to ensure uninterrupted power, construction or expansion of terminals and hangars to support emergency personnel and aircraft, modernization of fuel storage facilities, and airfield enhancements that increase capacity for staging supplies and coordinating response activities. The awards support the 
Western North Carolina Economic Recovery Plan
, the long-term framework Governor Josh Stein released in September for rebuilding and growing the region’s economy. The plan’s infrastructure line of effort calls for transportation and other systems that are “sized for growth, built to last, and designed on a regional basis.” The plan also identifies five of the grant recipients – the Ashe County, Avery County, Jackson County, Rutherford County, and Western Carolina Regional airports – among the region’s network of general aviation airports and calls for activating a regional air-access plan that spreads economic activity beyond Asheville.
